compatibility_contract.legacy_invocations: Every S0 through S4 invocation without --acquisition-profile remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
compatibility_contract.legacy_packed_behavior: The existing standard-local-s1 packed_object_database rejection remains required when the selector is absent.
compatibility_contract.selected_loose_behavior: The new selector accepts a repository whose required objects are all loose.
compatibility_contract.selected_packed_behavior: The new selector accepts the approved packed subset with no reachable loose fallback.
compatibility_contract.equivalence: For a fixed standard profile, repository identity, revision, source bytes, and controlled envelope, selected loose and packed materializations produce identical RFC 8785 semantic bytes, semantic hashes, inventory, evidence, graph, storage input, documents, and query results as applicable.

supported_subset.repository_kind: non-bare local worktree with a real direct .git directory
object_sources: repository-local paired pack v2 and index v2 files
ignored_non_authoritative_sidecars: multi-pack-index when complete paired indexes are present

catalog_contract.pack_id: the lowercase 40-hex identifier shared by one pack/index pair
catalog_contract.ordering: ascending unsigned UTF-8 bytes of pack_id
catalog_contract.discovery: enumerate once, validate entry kinds without following symlinks, sort, open every authoritative regular file once, and retain stable handles
catalog_contract.pairing: exactly one .pack and one .idx for each authoritative pack_id
catalog_contract.unknown_or_unsafe_entry: typed failure; never ignored through filename fallback
catalog_contract.concurrent_repack: stable success from one coherent handle set or retryable object_database_changed; never partial success or implicit retry

index_contract.fanout: monotonic and exactly counts the strictly ascending unique OID table
index_contract.object_ids: strictly ascending unsigned bytes with no duplicate row
index_contract.crc32: one big-endian CRC32 per represented packed entry
index_contract.offsets32: one big-endian value per OID; high bit selects the large-offset table
index_contract.offsets64: every referenced large-offset slot exists, is referenced exactly once, and names a candidate offset inside the pack entry region
index_contract.candidate_offset_policy: index validation proves bounds and uniqueness; every candidate must match one-to-one with the bounded sequential pack-entry map before revision resolution
index_contract.index_checksum: collision-detecting SHA-1 over all preceding index bytes

pack_contract.count: matches the validated index object count
pack_contract.trailer: collision-detecting SHA-1 over all preceding pack bytes
pack_contract.filename_binding: pack_id equals the pack trailer checksum
pack_contract.whole_pack_validation: every paired pack header and trailer checksum is validated before revision resolution
pack_contract.entry_map: starting at byte 12, consume exactly the pack-declared entry count; parse each header and delta-base header, inflate one exact zlib stream under per-entry and cumulative structural limits while discarding output, record start and end, validate inflated size and CRC, and require one-to-one equality with index offsets
pack_contract.entry_validation: every location selected by the reachable closure additionally validates delta semantics, reconstructed type and size, and collision-detecting Git object OID
pack_contract.unreachable_entry_validation: unreachable entries receive structural framing, zlib, size, CRC, and offset-map validation but no delta reconstruction, retained body, or semantic OID validation
pack_contract.unreachable_corruption: raw-byte corruption is caught by whole-pack checksum; semantic entry validation is required for the reachable closure

object_resolution.duplicate_policy: Every reachable location for one OID must reconstruct the same Git type and bytes; any invalid location or conflict fails rather than falling back.
object_resolution.missing_policy: object_missing only when the OID is absent from every approved local source
object_resolution.kind_policy: repository_inconsistent only after a valid object reconstructs with an incompatible Git kind
object_resolution.sha1_policy: Git object IDs and pack/index checksums use collision-detecting SHA-1; a detected collision fails as object_database_invalid sha1_collision

delta_contract.algorithm: iterative stack machine with explicit cycle detection and counters
delta_contract.ofs_delta: base distance is nonzero, overflow-safe, strictly before the delta entry, and within the same pack
delta_contract.ref_delta: base OID resolves only through approved local locations and never triggers fetch or repair
delta_contract.header: base size and result size variable integers are complete, bounded, and exact
delta_contract.copy: offset and size fields are overflow-safe and the complete copy range lies inside the base
delta_contract.insert: literal length is nonzero and complete
delta_contract.resource_accounting: depth, program bytes, instructions, intermediate bytes, cumulative work, locations, and cache bytes are charged before allocation or copy

limit_contract.effective_limit: minimum of every applicable inherited type-aware S1 limit and packed-parser ceiling
limit_contract.regular_file_blob: single_file_bytes 4194304 is checked before retained semantic body reconstruction or allocation; the prerequisite discard-only structural inflate is separately charged to inflated_entry_bytes and cumulative_entry_inflate_bytes
limit_contract.public_limit_context: maximum is the exact fixed value for the limit token and observed is exactly maximum + 1
limit_contract.large_boundary_method: bounded model or injected reader plus representative real-byte integration case

error_contract.safe_context: No absolute path, pack filename, source byte, malformed byte, environment value, credential, or secret is emitted.
error_contract.automatic_retry: forbidden for acceptance evidence; changed remains the original typed observation

failure_precedence: complete invocation validation including standard profile and acquisition selector before repository filesystem access

acceptance_tests.assertion: Loose, base-only pack, OFS_DELTA, REF_DELTA, and cross-pack/loose REF materializations of the same commit produce identical semantic bytes and hashes with no loose fallback in packed variants.
Pairing, sidecars, MIDX, promisor markers, entry kinds, ordering, duplicate locations, and transient catalog states match the fixed contract.
Magic, version, length, fanout, OID order, CRC table, 32/64-bit offsets, checksums, and object counts reject every reviewed mutation with the exact safe reason.
Header, version, count, trailer, filename, and index checksum binding are verified before revision resolution and publish nothing on failure.
Headers, exact zlib framing, CRC32, declared size, reconstructed kind/size, collision detection, and Git OID are all enforced.
Valid OFS chains resolve; zero, overflow, forward, missing, and out-of-pack distances fail deterministically.
Same-pack, cross-pack, and loose local bases resolve without fetch; absent or invalid bases fail.
Cycles, depth 51, oversized programs, excessive instructions/work, opcode zero, truncated inserts, out-of-range copies, and size mismatch terminate within every budget.
Every new limit has a successful maximum model and a typed maximum-plus-one result whose observed value is capped.
Fifty catalog/location permutations and ten shuffled parallel repetitions produce identical semantic bytes and failure precedence.
Rename, truncate, rewrite, and repack schedules produce one stable result or object_database_changed, never fallback, SIGBUS, panic, partial output, or accepted retry.
The inherited Linux gate observes no process, network, write, outside-root access, hook/filter/credential execution, or target sentinel event.
Separate catalog/index, pack-entry/zlib, and delta-machine seed corpora find no panic, unbounded allocation, loop, or unsafe behavior.
Offline differential results against Git strict validation and an independent reader are retained; every divergence is reviewed and neither tool can weaken the ratified oracle.
All accepted S0 through S4 fixtures, errors, semantic hashes, output roots, and the legacy packed rejection remain byte-identical without the selector.
